beats.label: S1 · New form, new feelings
beats.text: Charlie, secretly meeting bully Ben Hope, is seated next to rugby player Nick Nelson in his new form and develops feelings, unsure if Nick could ever be gay.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the Charlie/Nick/Ben triangle and Charlie's baseline that every later beat pulls from.

beats.label: S1 · Nick starts questioning
beats.text: Nick invites Charlie onto the rugby team; they grow close, and Nick tries to hold Charlie's hand while he sleeps, quietly questioning his own sexuality.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The private crack in Nick's assumed straightness — without it the kiss is unmotivated.

beats.label: S1 · Kiss and panic
beats.text: At Harry's birthday party, Nick and Charlie kiss in a back room, but Nick panics and flees when his rugby mates call for him, leaving Charlie heartbroken.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's pivot: closet vs feelings, and the shape of every conflict that follows.

beats.label: S1 · Secret dating begins
beats.text: Nick turns up at Charlie's door the next day; they agree to date in secret while Nick figures himself out, and he later realises he's bisexual.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Their real relationship starts here, on secrecy — the frame the rest of the series pushes against.

beats.label: S1 · Cinema and cruelty
beats.text: On a group cinema outing, Harry mocks Charlie's sexuality and Nick fights him for it, while Ben corners Charlie to tell him nobody could ever really care.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nick publicly picks Charlie in a fistfight and Ben's abuse peaks — both drive Charlie's collapse next.

beats.label: S1 · Charlie breaks, then chooses
beats.text: Depressed, Charlie quits rugby and shuts Nick out, but Nick and Tao bond over wanting him happy; Charlie confronts Ben for good and takes Nick back.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cuts Ben out of Charlie's life and locks Nick and Tao into being allies — both matter next season.

beats.label: S1 · Nick comes out to his mum
beats.text: On a seaside date, Nick tells Charlie he plans to come out to their friends; that same night, he tells his mum he has a boyfriend, and she accepts him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First rung of the coming-out ladder that structures the whole of Season 2.

cliffhanger.text: Nick and Charlie are a couple, and Nick has just come out to his mum with plans to tell their friends. His rugby mates, brother, father and the wider school still don't know, and Charlie's history with Ben has left scars neither has really talked about.
questions: How far is Nick actually willing to go in coming out?
Will Ben Hope really stay out of Charlie's life now?
Can Charlie and Tao's friendship survive the secret Charlie kept?

characters.name: Charlie Spring
characters.line: Bullied Truham student who escaped his manipulative ex Ben and is now, cautiously, in his first real relationship.

characters.name: Nick Nelson
characters.line: Rugby captain who realised he's bisexual through Charlie and has just come out to his mum, no one else.

characters.name: Tao Xu
characters.line: Charlie's fiercely protective best friend, hurt at being kept in the dark about Nick but reconciled by season's end.

characters.name: Elle Argent
characters.line: Charlie's trans friend, transferred to Higgs Girls after coming out, quietly in love with Tao.

characters.name: Ben Hope
characters.line: Charlie's closeted, controlling ex who used and manipulated him; finally cut off but still in the school.

characters.name: Imogen Heaney
characters.line: Nick's friend who liked him romantically and gracefully accepted his honesty about not liking her back.

characters.name: Tara Jones
characters.line: Out lesbian at Higgs who quietly mentored Nick through his questioning; dating Darcy.

characters.name: Darcy Olsson
characters.line: Tara's girlfriend, who calmed her down after homophobic comments at the orchestral concert.

characters.name: Harry Greene
characters.line: Nick's homophobic rugby friend, suspended after the cinema fight but still around at school.

beats.label: S2 · Coming out, one by one
beats.text: Nick starts coming out — first to Imogen, who reveals she's now dating Ben; Charlie's father learns of the relationship and bans Nick from the house.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kicks off Nick's season-long coming-out project and puts Ben back in orbit through Imogen.

beats.label: S2 · Tao afraid of losing Elle
beats.text: Tao grows jealous as Elle visits Lambert art school and befriends its crowd, terrified of losing her; his mum tells him to fight to keep her close.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Seeds the Tao/Elle romance and the future she's about to choose — both crucial to their arc next season.

beats.label: S2 · Paris turns the couples
beats.text: On the Paris trip, Imogen dumps Ben when she realises he still obsesses over Charlie, and Elle and Tao finally kiss after committing to try being more.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Ben's grip on the story and starts Tao/Elle in earnest — two threads that carry into Season 3.

beats.label: S2 · Truth or dare, two revelations
beats.text: In a hotel truth-or-dare, Nick comes out to the wider classroom crowd; separately, Isaac is kissed by James and realises he doesn't want anyone that way.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Nick's public coming-out step and the door opening on Isaac's asexuality — both pay off next season.

beats.label: S2 · Nick confronts his family
beats.text: Home from Paris, Nick confronts his bullying brother David and dismissive father, telling his father outright that Charlie is his boyfriend.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The last people Nick has to face; the fracture with David and his dad shapes S3's Christmas scenes.

beats.label: S2 · Out on Instagram, into prom
beats.text: Nick comes out publicly on Instagram; Elle picks Lambert and agrees to be Tao's girlfriend as the whole friend group heads to the school prom together.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes Nick's coming-out arc and pairs off Tao/Elle — the group's stable state going into the next season.

beats.label: S2 · What Charlie hasn't said
beats.text: After prom, Charlie tells Nick about the bullying that drove him to self-harm; walking home, he drafts a text saying 'I love you' but doesn't send it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two live threads that open Season 3: Charlie's fragile mental health and the unsaid love confession.

cliffhanger.text: Nick is fully out and their relationship is public and steady, but Charlie has just admitted to a history of self-harm and is walking home with an unsent 'I love you' on his phone. Nick has asked to be told when Charlie is stressed, and Charlie has promised.
questions: Will Charlie ever send that 'I love you'?
Is the self-harm really in Charlie's past?
Can Charlie keep his promise to tell Nick when he's struggling?

characters.name: Charlie Spring
characters.line: Publicly with Nick and back on the rugby team; carrying a history of self-harm he's only just started to share.

characters.name: Nick Nelson
characters.line: Fully out to family, friends and Instagram after a season of steadily coming out to everyone in his life.

characters.name: Tao Xu
characters.line: Now Elle's boyfriend, having worked through his jealousy of her new art-school world.

characters.name: Elle Argent
characters.line: Accepted into Lambert School of Art and dating Tao — new school and new relationship at once.

characters.name: Tara Jones
characters.line: In love with Darcy and finally hearing it back, after a rocky patch over Darcy's guardedness.

characters.name: Darcy Olsson
characters.line: Has just left her homophobic mother's house after a fight; struggling quietly behind the loud front.

characters.name: Isaac Henderson
characters.line: Realised through a kiss from James that he doesn't want anyone that way — coming to terms with being asexual.

characters.name: Imogen Heaney
characters.line: Newly single after dumping Ben over his fixation on Charlie; one of Nick's steady allies.

characters.name: Ben Hope
characters.line: Charlie's ex who tried to apologise seeking self-forgiveness and was refused; now leaving Truham.

beats.label: S3 · Love said, illness sensed
beats.text: At a beach day, Nick asks if Charlie has an eating disorder; Charlie denies it but later confesses his love face-to-face, and Nick returns it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fires the season's two engines at once: the love the couple is now openly in, and the illness driving it.

beats.label: S3 · Charlie unravels while Nick's away
beats.text: With Nick away in Menorca, Charlie unravels; his sister Tori alerts Nick, and Charlie admits over the phone that he may have an eating disorder.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The denial breaks and Tori steps in — the moment the family stops treating this as private.

beats.label: S3 · Push to get help
beats.text: Back at school, Nick and Tao push Charlie to tell his parents and seek treatment; Isaac comes out as aromantic and asexual, feeling adrift among couples.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Charlie's treatment path opens and Isaac's identity crystallises — both settle into what they'll carry forward.

beats.label: S3 · The clinic
beats.text: After months of decline and a self-harm relapse, Charlie is admitted to an inpatient clinic, is diagnosed with anorexia and OCD, and comes home by December.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The medical centre of gravity of the season and the reason Charlie's world looks different from here on.

beats.label: S3 · Christmas, two families
beats.text: Over Christmas, Charlie fights with his mother and flees to Nick's; Nick finally confronts his bullying brother David and names his father's absence.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Parallel family confrontations that reset both leads' relationships with the people they came from.

beats.label: S3 · Bodies, on their own terms
beats.text: On Charlie's birthday, body shame stops him having sex with Nick; weeks later, after another row at home, he goes to Nick's and they sleep together — shirt on.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The last intimacy barrier crossed at Charlie's pace — the couple's private threshold moment.

beats.label: S3 · Futures pull apart
beats.text: On a university road trip, Imogen comes out to Nick as gay, Tara sours on Oxford, and Nick quietly admits he prefers Leeds — futures start to diverge.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The whole group's next chapter takes shape here, including the geography that will separate Nick and Charlie.

cliffhanger.text: Charlie is months into recovery, sleeping over at Nick's, and the couple has crossed every intimacy threshold together. But sixth form is ending, Nick is leaning toward Leeds, and Charlie still has another year of school ahead.
questions: Can Charlie's recovery hold once Nick actually leaves?
Will Nick and Charlie survive being in different cities?
What does Imogen's coming out mean for who she becomes next?

characters.name: Charlie Spring
characters.line: Diagnosed with anorexia and OCD, months into recovery, deeply in love with Nick and back at school.

characters.name: Nick Nelson
characters.line: Has steadied Charlie through treatment while quietly favouring Leeds for university.

characters.name: Tori Spring
characters.line: Charlie's sharp older sister, the one who spotted the eating disorder and stayed close through recovery.

characters.name: Tao Xu
characters.line: Elle's boyfriend and one of Charlie's most active supports through the crisis.

characters.name: Elle Argent
characters.line: Studying at Lambert and in love with Tao, privately worried that sex could trigger gender dysphoria.

characters.name: Tara Jones
characters.line: Rethinking Oxford after visiting; still committed to Darcy.

characters.name: Darcy Olsson
characters.line: Living with Grandma Ivy after leaving home; exploring a non-binary identity.

characters.name: Isaac Henderson
characters.line: Openly aromantic and asexual, no longer trying to fit the group's coupled shape.

characters.name: Imogen Heaney
characters.line: Has just come out to Nick as gay after realising her attraction to men was performance.
